result:
I’ll trace scorer reconstruction and guardrail loading, then add the server-side restriction and focused tests. I’ll use the repository’s Python style skill for the changes.
The workspace already has regression tests staged for this change; I’ll preserve and use them. The current reconstruction code lets the opt-in flag enable execution in the server. I’ll make server loading return metadata, permit reconstruction in job execution, and reject custom guardrails before reconstruction.
The main changes are in place, and focused tests are running. I also found that disabled custom scorers need to be filtered before job submission; otherwise, the scheduler could abort before submitting built-in scorers. That check is now included.
All 42 selected regression tests passed, with two skipped. Pytest then hit a sandbox permission error in the repository’s resource-reporting hook. An earlier, broader run also hit tracing-fixture failures. I’m adding coverage for nested ensembles and inherited executor permission, then checking those cases and the existing guardrail behavior.
Implemented inert custom-scorer loading in the server, with reconstruction blocked and executor permission cleared at server startup. Client and job-executor behavior is preserved.

Custom guardrails—including ensembles—are rejected. Existing custom guardrails now cause a named server error; other loading failures remain logged and skipped.

Validation: 46 focused tests passed, 2 skipped. Earlier broader checks hit tracing-fixture and sandbox reporting errors. No dependencies installed.
